acceptance_criteria.criterion: With no stores.json present, index.ts starts successfully in single-store mode and getStoreRouter().isMultiStoreMode() returns false
With a valid stores.json, index.ts starts in multi-store mode and getStoreRouter().isMultiStoreMode() returns true
All configured store directories that do not exist are created during startup
migrateToNamespacedLayout() is called for each configured store path
getStoreRouter() throws a descriptive error if called before setStoreContext()
The entire existing test suite continues to pass without modification (no stores.json = legacy mode)

summary: Created mcp-server/src/storage/store-context.ts — shared singleton accessor following the client-info.ts pattern. Exports setStoreContext(), getStoreRouter(), and getMultiStoreManager(). Both getters throw a descriptive error if called before initialization.

Modified mcp-server/src/index.ts startup sequence: loads stores.json via loadStoresConfig() after resolveLedgerRoot(); constructs StoreRouter (legacy mode on null, multi-store mode on config); constructs MultiStoreManager; calls setStoreContext(); runs migrateToNamespacedLayout() on all configured store paths; resolves gui-config.json path via resolveGuiConfigPath(storeConfig, ledgerRoot).

Created mcp-server/tests/storage/store-context.test.ts with 8 tests covering: throw before init (both getters), singleton returns correct instances, legacy mode isMultiStoreMode()=false, multi-store mode isMultiStoreMode()=true, idempotent re-initialization, and store directory auto-creation.
Full test suite: 129 files / 3764 tests — all passing. TypeScript type check: clean.

comments.note: index.ts startup sequence is now async-heavier (loadStoresConfig adds an async file read before tool registration). In the current architecture this is fine since no tools are invoked until after main() resolves, but if startup latency ever becomes a concern the stores.json read could be parallelized with other async startup steps (e.g. discoverAgents, readConfigFromDisk) using Promise.all.

The store-context.ts module exposes module-level let state analogous to client-info.ts. Both modules follow the same pattern: set-once singletons reset between tests via setStoreContext(). The pattern is well-established and consistent across the codebase.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified. 8 targeted store-context tests pass. Full regression suite: 129 files / 3764 tests — all green. TypeScript type-check clean. store-context.ts singleton pattern is correct and consistent with client-info.ts. index.ts startup sequence correctly branches on storeConfig null/non-null, calls setStoreContext() before migration, and runs migrateToNamespacedLayout() for every store path.

comments.note: The 'before setStoreContext()' describe block relies on test ordering: the singleton is undefined only because those two tests run before any setStoreContext() call in the file. Vitest runs describe blocks sequentially so this is safe, but it would be more robust to use vi.resetModules() in a beforeEach to truly isolate the singleton state. Not a blocker — tests pass correctly and the ordering is documented.
No observations beyond the low-pri ordering note above — code is clean and consistent with the client-info.ts singleton pattern.

comments.note: store-context.test.ts line 1: added 'afterEach' to the explicit vitest import. The function was used via the globals:true fallback but every other storage test file in the project (14 files checked) imports it explicitly. Change is non-behavioral — all 8 tests continue to pass.

Test ordering fragility (already noted by QA): the 'before setStoreContext()' describe block relies on running before any setStoreContext() call in the file. This is safe because Vitest runs describe blocks sequentially and the ordering is documented in a comment. If the test suite grows significantly, exporting a test-only resetStoreContext() from store-context.ts (following the teardown pattern in other singletons) would provide true isolation without relying on ordering.
No observations beyond the above — implementation is clean, follows established patterns, and all acceptance criteria are verifiably met.
